reference: The club. The back room. The interrogation in the kitchen. This is the game's Sopranos wing.
diagnosis: The NPCs in this club are written well — the bartender is not a shelf, the slot machine attacked somebody, Snow likes the cold. The Prospect standing in front of them is written like a dialogue menu. Almost every weak line in this scene is his: 'What have you got?' 'I understand.' 'Noted for the record.' 'Good to see you too, Boosk.' He is the one character with nothing to say in a room where everybody else is specific. Second problem: the interrogation goes polite exactly when it should go cold — you do not ask a man you have just worked over with kitchen equipment why he didn't mention it sooner.

lines.current: Please don't make me a bit.
lines.why: CUT — 'a bit' is meta-comedy slang that acknowledges the game's own joke structure. Doctrine violation, same family as the Counter-Strike line.
lines.house: Whatever this is, I'm not doing it.
lines.tarantino: Whatever's about to happen, I want it in the record that I said no. Out loud. In front of people.
lines.mcdonagh: No. Whatever that is, no. I've seen your face doin' that before and it never ends well for me.
lines.houser: Absolutely not. Whatever this is, I decline, and I'd like that reflected in the minutes.
lines.coen: No. I don't — whatever this is, I'd rather not. Thank you, though.

lines.why: The single most generic tough-guy line available, said to Big Uncle Lou of all people, who would eat it.
lines.house: I've got it. I know how it looks. I've got it.
lines.tarantino: I know what I'm doing. And I know that's exactly what a man who doesn't know what he's doing says. I'm saying it anyway.
lines.mcdonagh: I know what I'm at. I know that's what an eejit says. I'm sayin' it regardless.
lines.houser: I've got a handle on it. And yes, I hear how that sounds, and no, I don't have a better sentence.
lines.coen: I know what I'm doing. I do. I've thought about it some.

lines.why: A confirm button. Lou has just warned him about something serious and the kid has no reaction to it.
lines.house: I hear you. I don't like it, but I hear you.
lines.tarantino: I understand. I want to be clear that understanding it and liking it are two different rooms, and I'm only standing in one of them.
lines.mcdonagh: I understand you. I don't have to be happy about it, but I understand you.
lines.houser: Understood. And noted. And filed somewhere I'm going to be looking at for a while.
lines.coen: I understand. I don't know that I agree. But I understand it.

lines.why: Default RPG bar dialogue. The bartender here has real personality; the kid should be talking to a person, not a vendor menu.
lines.house: What's good back there that isn't going to kill me?
lines.tarantino: What have you got that a man can drink standing up, without a conversation about it.
lines.mcdonagh: What've you got? And don't be showin' me the bottle with the dust on it, I've seen where that's been.
lines.houser: What's on offer that won't ruin my evening or my liver, in that order?
lines.coen: What've you got back there? I'm not fussy. I'd just rather not have the one from last time.

lines.why: Stock phrase with no world in it.
lines.house: Last one. I've got a thing.
lines.tarantino: One more. And then I've got a thing, and I'd rather do the thing with one in me than none.
lines.mcdonagh: One more and I'm away. I've a job on, and it's the kind you'd want a drink in you for.
lines.houser: One more for the commute. I've got an appointment that's going to require a certain flexibility of conscience.
lines.coen: One more, then I'll get going. I've got something I've got to do.

lines.current: Anything I should know before I go back there?
lines.why: Exposition-fishing. Video-gamey 'give me the quest info' phrasing.
lines.house: What kind of mood is he in back there?
lines.tarantino: Before I go back there. What's the weather like. And I'm asking a man who has watched a lot of people walk back there.
lines.mcdonagh: What's the form back there? You've watched a lot of fellas go through that door, you'd know.
lines.houser: Give me the room back there. Mood, headcount, and whether anybody's already unhappy before I make it worse.
lines.coen: Anything I ought to know before I head back? You'd know better than me.

lines.current: Good to see you too, Boosk.
lines.why: Courteous nothing against a loud, huge character. This relationship is the emotional spine of the whole game and this is a handshake.
lines.house: You smell like a fire in a butcher's, Boosk.
lines.tarantino: Good to see you too. You're louder than last time. I didn't think there was room for louder.
lines.mcdonagh: Good to see you and all. You've gotten louder. I didn't think that was available to you.
lines.houser: Good to see you, Boosk. You've somehow gotten bigger, which I was told was not physically possible.
lines.coen: Good to see you too, Boosk. You look — yeah. You look about the same.

lines.why: Filler, and it sits right beside 'Your slot machine attacked me,' which shows exactly how good this beat can be.
lines.house: I came straight in. Nobody stopped me, which I'd look into.
lines.tarantino: Came straight in. Nobody stopped me. Walked past four of your guys and a door that's supposed to be locked, and here I am.
lines.mcdonagh: Came straight in. Nobody stopped me. You'd want to look at that, or someone less lovely than me'll do the same.
lines.houser: I walked straight in. Past two doors and four employees. That's a security review right there and I'm giving it to you free.
lines.coen: I came right in. Nobody said anything. I thought that was worth mentioning.

lines.why: Corporate-sounding acknowledgment. Ape is the best-written character in the game and deserves a scene partner.
lines.house: I'll write that on my hand.
lines.tarantino: Noted. Filed. Alphabetised. I'll be carrying that one around for a while.
lines.mcdonagh: Noted. That's goin' straight in the vault with the rest of your wisdom.
lines.houser: Noted, logged, and added to the growing document of things you've said to me that I'll need therapy about.
lines.coen: Noted. I'll remember that. I remember most of what you say, actually.

lines.why: Butler politeness from a mob prospect to a doorman.
lines.house: Then I'll be quick and he won't have to look at me long.
lines.tarantino: Then I won't keep him. I'll be in and out so fast he'll think he imagined it.
lines.mcdonagh: Then I'll not keep him. I'll be in and gone before he's finished disapprovin' of me.
lines.houser: Then I'll be brief. Nobody's ever complained that I took up too little of their evening.
lines.coen: Then I won't keep him long. I know he's busy. Everybody's busy.

lines.current: You look like you haven't slept.
lines.why: Bland table-setting. Aubbie is running herself into the ground; the observation should be specific and a little cruel, which is how people in this world show they care.
lines.house: You look like you've been awake since Tuesday and lost the argument.
lines.tarantino: You've got the face. The one people get around hour forty. I've seen it on men doing much worse work than this.
lines.mcdonagh: You look shockin'. I mean that kindly. You look like somethin' that's been left out.
lines.houser: You look like an HR case that hasn't been filed yet. Does this place have a maximum shift or is that just a thing other businesses have?
lines.coen: You look like you haven't slept. I don't mean anything by it. You just — you look like that.

lines.why: Toothless concern. It should be affection expressed the only way anyone in this family knows how — as an instruction with a threat shape.
lines.house: Go home, Aubbie. I'll tell him you were here till two and he can argue with me about it.
lines.tarantino: Go home. And if anybody asks where you went, they can come find me, and I'll explain it to them at length.
lines.mcdonagh: Go home to bed. And if anyone gives out about it, send them to me and I'll give out back at them.
lines.houser: Go home, Aubbie. Sleep is not a benefit this organization offers, so you'll have to steal it like everything else.
lines.coen: Get some sleep, Aubbie. Go on. Somebody's got to be the one who says it.

lines.why: Stock interrogation. Every other option in this beat has specificity — the hair, the silver case, the car — and this one has none.
lines.house: Whose money is in your shoes?
lines.tarantino: Let's start with money. Not names — money. Who paid you, how, and did it clear.
lines.mcdonagh: Who's payin' you? And don't say a name, say an amount. The amount tells me the name.
lines.houser: Who's funding you? And I want the entity, not the individual, because the individual's always some idiot with a clipboard.
lines.coen: Who hired you? I'd like to know that. It'd save everybody some time.

lines.current: Who sent you into our city?
lines.why: 'Our city' reads like a placeholder from a different, worse game.
lines.house: Who put you on a plane to this shithole?
lines.tarantino: Somebody put you on a plane. Somebody looked at a map, found this place, and thought: him. I want that person's name and I want to know what they were drinking.
lines.mcdonagh: Who sent you here? To here. Have you seen here? Someone hated you enough to send you here.
lines.houser: Who deployed you? Because somebody sat in an office and decided this town was worth an operative, and I'd love to see that business case.
lines.coen: Who sent you out here? Somebody had to send you. Nobody comes here on their own.

lines.current: Who inside the family are you talking to?
lines.why: Generic phrasing for the single most important question in the scene.
lines.house: Which one of ours has been talking to you? Say the name and this stops.
lines.tarantino: Somebody in that room upstairs has been talking to you. I've eaten with those men. I want a name, and then I want to go and sit down.
lines.mcdonagh: Which of ours is talkin' to you? I've had me dinner with every one of them. Say a name and ruin me evenin'.
lines.houser: Who's your inside line? Because I've got a room full of people upstairs and one of them's a subscription service.
lines.coen: Who're you talking to inside? Somebody is. That's just — that's the only way any of this works.

lines.current: Why didn't you tell us before?
lines.why: Curiously polite, immediately after torturing a confession out of a man. The kid should be cold here, or genuinely rattled — not conversational.
lines.house: You had that in you the whole time. All of that, for that.
lines.tarantino: You had that the whole time. That whole name was sitting in you while we did all of this. I want you to think about how much of the last hour was optional.
lines.mcdonagh: You had that in you the whole time. All that carry-on, and it was in you the whole while. That's on you, that is.
lines.houser: That was available the entire time. Every minute of the last hour was elective. I hope you understand that's a choice you made.
lines.coen: You had that the whole time. Huh. That's — that's a hell of a thing to sit on.

lines.why: Flat command sitting next to genuinely great options — the tongs, the ice bucket, the meat tenderiser. This one should be a choice with a reason in it.
lines.house: Cart stays where it is. He can look at it.
lines.tarantino: Leave the cart. Let him look at it. A man looking at a cart does more work in five minutes than I could do in an hour.
lines.mcdonagh: Leave the cart. Let him have a good look at it. That's half the job done and I've not lifted a thing.
lines.houser: Cart stays. Let him inventory it himself. Anticipation is free and I'm running a business.
lines.coen: Leave the cart alone. Just let him see it. That's usually enough, in my experience.

lines.why: A soft check-in with no edge and no humour, in a scene built entirely on kitchen-equipment menace.
lines.house: You still with us, Numbskull? Blink if the answer's no.
lines.tarantino: You holding up? And be honest, because there's a lot of night left and I need to know what I'm working with.
lines.mcdonagh: Are you alive in there, Numbskull? Give us a blink if you're not.
lines.houser: How are we doing, Numbskull? And I mean that operationally, not emotionally, because we don't do emotionally down here.
lines.coen: You holding up okay, Numbskull? It's been a long one. For everybody.

lines.current: Did you go through it properly?
lines.why: Managerial check-in tone in a room where a man is tied to a chair.
lines.house: Did you actually go through it, or did you look at it and get bored?
lines.tarantino: Did you go through it properly. And I want you to understand that 'properly' in this room means seams, shoes, and the lining, not a glance and a shrug.
lines.mcdonagh: Did you go through it right? Or did you have a wee look and lose interest, like you do.
lines.houser: Did you conduct an actual search, or the thing you do where you pat a bag and call it due diligence?
lines.coen: Did you go through it all the way? Because last time you went through it, you didn't go through it.

lines.why: Interchangeable with any heist scene in any game.
lines.house: Anything on there worth the night we're having?
lines.tarantino: Anything on there worth what this has cost us? And I'm counting the towels.
lines.mcdonagh: Is there anythin' on it worth the state of this room?
lines.houser: Is there anything of value on it, or have we destroyed a functioning kitchen for a man's holiday photos?
lines.coen: Anything on there worth anything? Because this has been a lot of trouble already.

lines.why: Purely functional information-gathering, in a scene whose whole comic engine is treating an interrogation like a cooking show.
lines.house: What have you tried so far, and why is it all still on the counter?
lines.tarantino: Walk me through what you've already tried. In order. Because from where I'm standing it looks like you've tried everything at once, which isn't a method, it's a mess.
lines.mcdonagh: What've you tried so far? And be honest, because I can see the counter and the counter's tellin' me a story.
lines.houser: What's been attempted so far? Give me the process. I'd like to know whether we're being systematic or just enthusiastic.
lines.coen: What have you tried already? I just don't want to repeat anything. That'd be a waste.

lines.current: Why can't you do this yourself?
lines.why: Flat and functional with no attitude behind it.
lines.house: Why is this mine? You've got two hands and a whole kitchen.
lines.tarantino: Explain to me why this is my job. You have two hands, a full kitchen, and about forty years on me.
lines.mcdonagh: Why's it me? You've the hands. You've the kitchen. You've the years. Why's it always me?
lines.houser: Why is this being delegated to me? You have the tools, the expertise, and, I'd argue, the temperament.
lines.coen: Why can't you do it yourself? I'm asking sincerely. You seem better suited.

lines.why: A non-answer with no payoff.
lines.house: They're alive, which this week counts.
lines.tarantino: They're alright. Which this month is a genuinely impressive answer.
lines.mcdonagh: They're grand. Well. They're breathin'. That's what grand means now.
lines.houser: They're fine. And by fine I mean nobody's in a hole, which is the current standard.
lines.coen: They're all right. Everybody's — yeah. Everybody's all right.

lines.current: You want them to turn the heat up?
lines.why: Weak small talk that wastes Snow's setup — Snow says it's cold in here and likes it. The comeback should engage the strangeness.
lines.house: You like it cold. That's a whole thing about you, isn't it.
lines.tarantino: You like it cold. I've noticed that. You're the only man I know who books a table by temperature.
lines.mcdonagh: You like it freezin'. That's not normal. I'm not sayin' it's wrong, I'm sayin' it's not normal.
lines.houser: You actually like it cold. That's not a preference, that's a condition, and I'd like it looked at.
lines.coen: You like it cold. Huh. Most people don't. But you do.

lines.current: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait.
lines.why: Plain relay with none of this bartender's flavour — the same man says 'I am not a shelf' and 'it makes the hands weird'.
lines.house: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait, and he said it in the voice.
lines.tarantino: Lou's in the back. He said don't make him wait. He said it twice, and the second time he said it to nobody, which is how I knew he meant it.
lines.mcdonagh: Lou's out the back. He said don't be keepin' him. And he'd the face on, so.
lines.houser: Lou's in the back. His exact words were don't make him wait, and his exact tone was the one that ends careers.
lines.coen: Lou's in the back. He said not to make him wait. I'd take him at his word on that.

lines.why: Functional question that undersells the tension of a briefing happening somewhere it should not be happening.
lines.house: Why are we doing this out here, where anybody can see us doing it?
lines.tarantino: Why here? There's forty people out that door and a girl on a pole eight feet from your head. Why is this the room you picked.
lines.mcdonagh: Why here? There's half the county out that door. Why's this the room you chose for it?
lines.houser: Why are we having this conversation here? There's a public on the other side of that curtain and a camera in the corner I don't recognise.
lines.coen: Why're you giving me this here? There's people right out there. That's all I'm saying.

lines.why: Flat and incurious, delivered immediately after a brutal beating at the party. The kid does not react at all to what just happened.
lines.house: What's in room twelve? And don't tell me on the way, tell me now, because I've had a night.
lines.tarantino: What's in room twelve. And before you answer — I've just watched a man get taken apart at a party. So take your time and pick your words, because I'm not in a good place for a surprise.
lines.mcdonagh: What's in room twelve? And say it now, not in the car. I've had enough of findin' things out in cars.
lines.houser: What's in room twelve? And I'd like the full brief, not the version where I find out the important part while I'm holding something.
lines.coen: What's at room twelve? I'd like to know before we go. That's not — I don't think that's unreasonable.

lines.why: A mob-club dealer apologising undercuts the house's cold energy, which the sibling line ('The house always liked me better') gets right.
lines.house: That's a bust. The house doesn't feel anything about it.
lines.tarantino: Bust. And I want you to know I felt nothing. Twenty-two years, and I have never once felt anything.
lines.mcdonagh: Bust. I'd say I'm sorry but I'd be lyin' and we've enough of that in here.
lines.houser: Bust. The house thanks you for your contribution to the renovation fund.
lines.coen: That's a bust. Yeah. These things happen.

scene: The Enola Squatch / PROJECT SILENT SQUATCH
reference: The war-film bombing raid, and the Manhattan Project. A basement full of borrowed scientists builds a bomb for a jerky cartel, and then the cartel does what cartels do with people who know things.
diagnosis: Two failures. The bomb-run lines reach for the shooter one-liner ('Hope they're hungry', 'Lou sends his regards') at the exact moment the scene has earned dread instead. And every scientist dies in stock hostage-movie language — 'We have families!', 'Please!' — after being written with real specificity ten minutes earlier. Men who spent twelve weeks arguing about shielding do not die in a disaster film. They die mid-argument, still trying to be useful, because being useful is the only currency they have ever had.

lines.why: Reads like the kid is reading the label off the ordnance. It is the moment he drops it; it should cost him something or reveal something ugly about him.
lines.house: Fat Squatch away. God help whoever's down there.
lines.tarantino: You know they named it. Somebody in a basement sat down and named this thing. Fat Squatch. Like it's a horse.
lines.mcdonagh: Fat Squatch, away. Christ. Somebody named it. Somebody sat down and thought about a name.
lines.houser: Fat Squatch is away. Product delivered. Somebody in marketing is going to be very pleased with themselves.
lines.coen: There it goes. The Fat Squatch. That's — yeah. That's what they called it.

lines.why: The single most-used one-liner in the history of the medium. It also winks, which the doctrine forbids.
lines.house: It's gone. It's out. Turn us the hell around.
lines.tarantino: It's away. Don't look. I'm telling you as a friend, do not look down.
lines.mcdonagh: It's gone. Don't look at it. I'm serious now, don't look at it.
lines.houser: Payload's away. Whatever's down there just became somebody else's paperwork.
lines.coen: It's away. Okay. That's — okay. That's done now.

lines.why: Second-hand gangster-movie catchphrase. It also makes a mass casualty event sound like a slap.
lines.house: That's from Lou. All of it. Every bit of it is from Lou.
lines.tarantino: That's Lou's. I want that on the record. That's Lou's, all the way down.
lines.mcdonagh: That's from Lou. And I'll be sayin' that in me sleep for the rest of me life, so I will.
lines.houser: Compliments of Big Uncle Lou. Who is, and I want this noted, four hundred miles away eating a sandwich.
lines.coen: That one's from Lou. I'd want them to know that, if there was anybody left to tell.

lines.why: A joke at the exact frame the scene must not joke. Wrong on the doctrine and wrong on the character.
lines.house: Bay's clear. I'd like to stop being the guy who did this now.
lines.tarantino: Bay's clear. And I want you to know I'm going to remember exactly where I was standing.
lines.mcdonagh: That's it gone. And I'll be honest with you — I don't feel a thing. Which is worse, I think. That's the bit that'll get me.
lines.houser: Payload away, bay's clear, and I have just personally out-produced every drone strike in the Pacific Northwest.
lines.coen: That's it out. Huh. I thought I'd feel something. I don't, really.

lines.why: The euphemism is right in principle — Lou would absolutely call it a package — but it is said so mildly it reads as shipping and receiving instead of a man asking whether a town is still there.
lines.house: Did it land where I paid for it to land?
lines.tarantino: So. Did they take delivery? And I want the real answer, not the one you rehearsed in the car.
lines.mcdonagh: Did they get it? And don't be soft with me now. Did they get it.
lines.houser: Did the package arrive? And by arrive I mean is there anybody left down there to have received it.
lines.coen: They get the package all right? I only ask because I've heard two versions already and they don't agree.

lines.why: A delivery-driver gag on a mass-casualty report. It undercuts, and worse, the kid should not be joking yet — he has not landed emotionally.
lines.house: There's nothing down there to sign anything.
lines.tarantino: They got it. There's a hole where the road used to bend. I flew over the same ground twice looking for the bend.
lines.mcdonagh: They got it, aye. There's a hole in the ground the shape of a town and I'll be seein' it every time I close me eyes.
lines.houser: Delivered. Signed for by nobody, because signing requires hands.
lines.coen: They got it. There's — there's not a lot down there now. I don't know what else to tell you about it.

lines.current: Good. Put the plane back where you found it.
lines.why: This one is actually close to great — the banality is the joke, and the doctrine likes that. It just needs to be said by somebody who has already moved on, which is what makes it obscene.
lines.house: Good. Put the plane back where you found it and wash the smell out of your coat before dinner.
lines.tarantino: Good. Now put the plane back exactly where you found it, and I mean exactly, because the man I borrowed it from counts things.
lines.mcdonagh: Grand. Put the plane back. And wipe your boots, you've the whole state on 'em.
lines.houser: Excellent. Return the aircraft to inventory, and I want it in the condition you took it, because that lease is in my sister's name.
lines.coen: Good. Well. Put the plane back where you got it. And, you know — take a shower. You look like something.

lines.why: Textbook disaster-movie plea. She has been the sharpest voice in the basement for twelve weeks and she dies as an extra.
lines.house: I have a daughter in Kyiv who thinks I'm dead already. Do not make her right.
lines.tarantino: I have a daughter. She is nineteen. She thinks I am dead — I let her think that, because it was safer for her, and I would very much like to be able to correct that at some point.
lines.mcdonagh: I've a daughter. She thinks I'm dead. I let her think it. And now you're goin' to make an honest woman of me, is that it?
lines.houser: I have a daughter, a mother, and a lease. Any one of those is more paperwork for you than a bullet is.
lines.coen: I have a family. I don't know if that matters to you. It probably doesn't. But I wanted it said out loud.

lines.why: Nobody in a locked room bargains with a promise. She should bargain with the only thing she owns — what is in her head.
lines.house: Who would we tell? Who on this earth would believe one word of it?
lines.tarantino: Tell who? Think about what you are afraid of for one second. We would have to explain the sasquatch. Nobody gets past the sasquatch.
lines.mcdonagh: Tell who? Who'd believe us? We'd have to start with the fuckin' sasquatch and we'd be in a home by teatime.
lines.houser: We have no one to tell. We are undocumented, unpaid, and technically deceased in two countries. You built the perfect workforce and now you're destroying the asset.
lines.coen: We wouldn't tell anybody. Who would we tell? Nobody'd believe a word of it, that's the — that's the whole thing.

lines.why: Generic. Vetrov's whole character is that he solves the problem in front of him; his plea should be a proposal, delivered too fast, with numbers in it.
lines.house: We can build you another one. Smaller. Eight weeks. Six if you stop asking about the shielding.
lines.tarantino: You want another one? We can build you another one. Smaller, cleaner, half the shielding, eight weeks — six, if nobody comes down here to ask me how it's going. That is a better use of me than a hole in the ground.
lines.mcdonagh: We'll build you another. A better one. A smaller one. I'll do it in eight weeks and I'll not complain once, which for me is a fuckin' miracle.
lines.houser: You have a functioning R&D division standing in front of you and you're about to fire all of it in one go. That's not security, that's a write-off.
lines.coen: We could work for you. That's — I mean, we already do. We've been doing that. So.

lines.why: One word of nothing on a death beat. Even a man out of arguments has one specific last one.
lines.house: Please. Please. I did the shielding right. I did the shielding right and nobody even checked.
lines.tarantino: Please. I got the shielding right. Nobody checked. Nobody ever came down and checked, and I got it right anyway. That should count. Somewhere, that should count.
lines.mcdonagh: Please. Please now. I did it right. I did every bit of it right and not one of yiz ever came down to look.
lines.houser: Please. I have been very reasonable about a great many things in this basement and I would like that considered.
lines.coen: Please. I'm asking. I don't have anything better than that. I'm just asking.

lines.why: Boilerplate. Sokolov was shouting 'Twelve weeks!' in triumph minutes ago — his plea should be the same pride, souring in real time.
lines.house: Twelve weeks. You said impossible and we did it in twelve weeks and this is the room you put us in.
lines.tarantino: Twelve weeks. You stood in that doorway and said it could not be done, and we did it in twelve weeks, on your food, with your lights going off every night at ten. And this is the room. This is the room you had picked out the whole time.
lines.mcdonagh: Twelve weeks! We did it in twelve fuckin' weeks and you'd the room picked out before we started, didn't you. You'd it picked out.
lines.houser: We delivered ahead of schedule, under budget, in a basement, on a diet of jerky, and this is the exit package.
lines.coen: We did everything you asked. Twelve weeks. And I guess that was — I guess that was the problem, wasn't it.

lines.current: You cannot leave us in here!
lines.why: Stage direction. It states the situation instead of reacting to it.
lines.house: There is no air in here. You know that. Somebody in this building did that math and it was probably me.
lines.tarantino: There's no air in this room. I know because I calculated it. Third week. For fun. That is the joke — I did the math on my own room and I laughed.
lines.mcdonagh: There's no air in here! I worked that out meself, weeks ago, for a laugh! For a fuckin' laugh!
lines.houser: This room has no ventilation. I flagged that in writing. There is a memo. There is a memo about this exact room.
lines.coen: You can't leave us in here. There's no air. I did that math myself, which is — that's a hell of a thing, when you think about it.

lines.why: Expository shock. A man watching his colleague die does not narrate it as a question to the room.
lines.house: He was standing right there. He wasn't even — he had a pen in his hand.
lines.tarantino: He had a pen in his hand. He was writing something down. Whatever it was, that was the last thing he thought was important, and now nobody will ever know what it was.
lines.mcdonagh: He'd a pen in his hand. He was writin' somethin' down. What was he writin'? Somebody tell me what he was writin'.
lines.houser: He was mid-sentence. You shot a man mid-sentence. Do you understand how much unfinished work is on that desk?
lines.coen: He was just standing there. He had a pen. I don't — why would you do that to a man with a pen?

lines.why: Off-the-shelf villain speak. Booski is funnier and colder than this everywhere else in the game.
lines.house: He's done. There's nothing left in him that Lou paid for.
lines.tarantino: Here's the thing about a specialist. The day the thing is built, the specialist becomes a guy who knows how you built it. That's not a demotion. That's a whole different job, and it's one nobody's hiring for.
lines.mcdonagh: He's finished. He's not a scientist any more, he's a witness with a doctorate.
lines.houser: He's transitioned from an asset to a liability. That happened at approximately four this afternoon and nobody sent him the memo.
lines.coen: He's done being useful. That's just where we're at with him now.

lines.why: The most generic order a crime boss can give, and it is then repeated almost verbatim as the actual kill order.
lines.house: Lock it. All of it. Both doors.
lines.tarantino: Lock the door. Then lock the other door. Then go upstairs and be somewhere else for about an hour.
lines.mcdonagh: Lock it. And don't stand there listenin' — that's how fellas get strange.
lines.houser: Secure the room. And nobody makes a note of the time, because a time is the kind of detail that ends up in a courtroom.
lines.coen: Go ahead and lock it up. Both of them. Then come on upstairs.

lines.why: The pivotal beat of the whole scene lands on a repeat of the previous cliché. This is the line that has to make the player's stomach drop.
lines.house: I said do it. Don't make me the guy who says it a third time, kid — that guy remembers.
lines.tarantino: I said do it. And now I've said it twice, which means from here on it isn't an order any more, it's a test. You understand the difference? Because the difference is your whole life.
lines.mcdonagh: I said do it. That's twice now. There isn't a third one, and you'll not like the shape of what comes instead.
lines.houser: I gave you an instruction. Now I've given it again, which is already a performance issue, and I'd hate for this to become a conversation about you.
lines.coen: I said handle it. That's the second time I've said it. I don't generally get to a third.

lines.why: Flat confirmation. Booski has crude color everywhere else and none of it here.
lines.house: You're certain. Say it like a man who has to live in the same state as this thing.
lines.tarantino: Certain. Not confident, not optimistic — certain. Because I'm going to repeat your answer to a man upstairs, word for word, and he doesn't take confident.
lines.mcdonagh: You're certain, are you? Because I'm the fella that has to go up them stairs and say it, and I'd rather not be wrong in front of him.
lines.houser: Certain, or certain enough to sign? Because upstairs those are two very different products.
lines.coen: You're certain about that. Because I'm going to repeat it upstairs, and I'd rather repeat something true.

lines.why: A one-word shrug at the completion of a weapon. The game's biggest reveal deserves a reaction with a body in it.
lines.house: Good. Then that's the thing that's under my house now.
lines.tarantino: Good. So there it is. Twelve weeks, four Russians and a basement, and now there's a thing under Lou's house that can end a town. And we're all going to go upstairs and eat.
lines.mcdonagh: Good. Grand. There's a bomb under the house. And we'll all go up now and have our dinner, will we.
lines.houser: Good. So we're now a jerky company with a strategic deterrent. I'd love to see how the accountant files that.
lines.coen: Good. Well. That's a hell of a thing to have under a house.

lines.why: Stock NPC bark. The sibling guard line ('The door stays open. I stay here. That's the arrangement.') proves the scene knows how to write these.
lines.house: Keep walking. Whatever you heard down here, you heard the boiler.
lines.tarantino: Keep walking. And whatever you think you heard — that's the boiler. It's a very old boiler. It does that.
lines.mcdonagh: Keep walkin'. That's the boiler. It's always the boiler. Everythin' down here is the boiler.
lines.houser: Keep moving. This corridor is not a place where people stop, and men who stop here become a topic.
lines.coen: Keep walking, please. That noise is the boiler. It's an old building.

lines.why: Two words with no man attached to them.
lines.house: Back up. I don't get told what's in there either, and I've stopped wanting to know.
lines.tarantino: Back up. I've stood at this door eleven weeks. I don't know what's behind it, I've stopped guessing, and I'd advise you to arrive at the same place faster than I did.
lines.mcdonagh: Back up. I don't know what's in there and I've made me peace with not knowin', which took some doin'.
lines.houser: Step back. My clearance ends at this door, my curiosity ended about a month before that.
lines.coen: Back up, please. I don't know what's in there. I've decided that's fine.

lines.current: Eh. You'll find out soon enough.
lines.why: Stock mysterious-boss filler, sitting next to genuinely great Lou writing ('It's a desk, kid, it's been there longer than you have').
lines.house: You'll find out. And then you'll wish you'd enjoyed not knowing more than you did.
lines.tarantino: You'll find out. And here's the part nobody warns you about — the not knowing was the good part. Right now, this, standing here annoyed at me. This is the good part.
lines.mcdonagh: You'll find out soon enough. And you'll wish to God you were back stood there botherin' me about it.
lines.houser: You'll be briefed. And when you are, you'll spend the rest of your life wishing you'd been slightly less curious in my office.
lines.coen: You'll find out. And then you'll have found out. That's how that goes.

lines.current: Welcome, brother. My initiation was worse. Everybody says that. Mine actually was.
lines.why: The line itself is good. The problem is it is copy-pasted across five named characters, which turns a party of individuals into one NPC with five faces. It needs four rewrites, not four tones — so the variants below are per-character, not per-director.
lines.house: [eric] Welcome, brother. Mine was worse. Everybody says that. Mine actually was.
lines.tarantino: [gratin] Welcome to it. Mine was worse. And before you say everybody says that — everybody does say that, and in my case it's documented.
lines.mcdonagh: [snow] Congratulations. Mine was worse. I'll not be describin' it. Not tonight, not ever, not to you.
lines.houser: [lou2] Welcome aboard. Mine was worse, and there's no HR here to tell it to, so it just lives in me.
lines.coen: [booski] Welcome, brother. Mine was worse. I know everybody says that. But I've got photographs.

lines.why: Same duplication problem, and the toast itself is a stock fantasy-tavern line. Five people raising a glass should raise five different glasses.
lines.house: [eric] To the new blood!
lines.tarantino: [gratin] To the kid. May he stay useful longer than the last one.
lines.mcdonagh: [snow] To the new fella. God love him, he's no idea.
lines.houser: [lou2] To the newest member of the organization, and to whoever ends up cleaning up after him.
lines.coen: [booski] To the new blood. And to the old blood. There's been a lot of both this year.

lines.current: You alright? You keep looking at Booski. We all love him but you're — you're really looking at him.
lines.why: A genuinely ominous piece of foreshadowing, destroyed by being said identically by five people. It should land once, from the one person drunk enough to say it.
lines.house: [eric] You alright? You keep looking at Booski. We all love him. But you're really looking at him.
lines.tarantino: [gratin] You keep looking at Booski. Not looking at him like a man looks at a friend. Looking at him like a man checks a room for exits.
lines.mcdonagh: [snow] You've been eyein' Booski all night. Now, we all love Booski. But that's not lovin', what you're doin'.
lines.houser: [lou2] You've had eyes on Booski for an hour. I'm not asking why. I'm telling you that I'm not the only one who noticed.
lines.coen: [booski himself, from behind] You keep looking at me. All night. I don't mind. I'm just saying I noticed, is all.

lines.current: You made it look easy. It's not easy. Ask the shirt by the truck. …too soon. Have a beer.
lines.why: The 'shirt by the truck' runner is the best joke in the party and duplication flattens it. Let each mouth land a different piece of it.
lines.house: [eric] You made it look easy. It's not. Ask the shirt by the truck. …Too soon. Have a beer.
lines.tarantino: [gratin] You made that look easy. It is not easy. There's a shirt by that truck could tell you how not easy, except a shirt can't talk, which is sort of the point I'm making.
lines.mcdonagh: [snow] You made it look easy. It isn't. Ask the shirt by the truck. …Ah. Too soon. Drink that.
lines.houser: [lou2] You made it look effortless, which is the worst thing you could have done, because now they'll expect it. Ask the shirt by the truck how expectations went for him.
lines.coen: [booski] You made it look easy. It isn't easy. There's a shirt by the truck. I won't say more than that.

scene: NO WAKE / MANSION UNDER SIEGE / Squatch Graveyard / The Silver Case
reference: NO WAKE is the Big Pussy boat episode. The Siege is the Scarface last stand. The Silver Case is Pulp Fiction. The Graveyard is the burial.
diagnosis: These four are the strongest writing in the game and mostly do not need help. The Silver Case in particular is the benchmark — 'Does he look like a bitch?', 'Congratulations. You've been promoted to witness.', 'You don't get to want it and not do it.' — that is the register the rest of the game should be measured against. NO WAKE is close behind and its problem is the opposite of everywhere else: it is so clipped that Willy, the man being killed, barely gets to beg. A man who knows he is about to die on a boat gets loud, gets undignified, and brings up things nobody wants brought up. That is the crudest and most human beat available and the scene currently skips it. The Siege drops a straight movie-quote ('Say hello to my little friend') which is the one thing the doctrine forbids — that is the scene pointing at its own reference.

lines.current: Say hello to my little friend.
lines.why: DOCTRINE VIOLATION — a direct, verbatim quote of the film being parodied. The tone doc's rule is that the player supplies the recognition and the scene never points at it. Quoting the line out loud hands the joke to the audience and kills it. The recognition is already fully delivered by the staging: a man on a landing with a mounted weapon and forty men on the lawn.
lines.house: [cut — let the gun be the line] All right. All right, come on then.
lines.tarantino: Okay. Okay. Everybody come up the stairs at once, then. All of you. Let's get it over with.
lines.mcdonagh: Right. Come on. Come on up, the whole fuckin' lot of yiz.
lines.houser: Fine. Everybody at once. Let's find out how many of you this thing was designed for.
lines.coen: Okay. All right then. Come on up.

lines.current: I don't remember every gun from every round.
lines.why: This is the moment Willy realises he is dead, and it is a reasonable, calm sentence. It is the last defensible thing he says before the scene turns, and it should be the sound of a man's story coming apart in his own mouth.
lines.house: I don't remember every gun from every round. Nobody remembers every — you're doing this over a gun?
lines.tarantino: I don't remember every gun from every round. Nobody does. You want me to remember a Negev from four years ago? Ask me what I had for breakfast. Go on. Ask me. I don't know that either, and nobody's ever killed a man over breakfast.
lines.mcdonagh: I don't remember every gun from every round! Who does? Who in the name of God remembers that? You don't. You're doin' this over a gun you don't remember either!
lines.houser: I don't recall every weapon from every round of a game we played four years ago, and I'd like somebody in this cabin to acknowledge how insane that sentence is.
lines.coen: I don't remember every gun. From every round. That's — nobody remembers that. That's not a thing people remember.

lines.current: Boosk, come on. You know me.
lines.why: Too dignified. This is his one appeal to the only man on the boat who loves him, and it should be undignified — that is what makes it unbearable.
lines.house: Boosk. Boosk, look at me. You were at my mother's funeral. You carried her. You carried her.
lines.tarantino: Boosk. Look at me. You were at my mother's funeral. You carried the box. You stood in the rain and you carried the box and you didn't complain once, and now you're standing there letting this happen in front of you.
lines.mcdonagh: Boosk. Boosk, look at me. You carried me mother's coffin. You did. You stood in the rain and you carried it. And now you'll stand there and watch this?
lines.houser: Boosk. You've known me eleven years. You were at my mother's funeral, you were at my wedding, you've slept on my floor. Somebody in this room say something.
lines.coen: Boosk. Come on. You know me. You've known me a long time. That's got to count for something. Doesn't it?

lines.why: The right instinct — a small dignity request. But it plays as polite where it should play as a man's legs going.
lines.house: Can I sit? I need to sit down. My legs have gone.
lines.tarantino: Can I sit down. I'm not asking for anything. I'm asking to sit down, because my legs have gone and I don't want to go down in front of you.
lines.mcdonagh: Can I sit? I need to sit. Me legs are gone and I'll not be goin' down in front of yiz.
lines.houser: Can I sit down? That's the whole ask. I'd like to do this sitting down, if that's available.
lines.coen: Can I take a seat? I'd — my legs aren't right. I'd rather sit.

lines.current: You were like a brother to me.
lines.why: The one cliché in an otherwise excellent scene. 'Like a brother' is the single most-used line in mob cinema and the past tense does all the work already.
lines.house: I had you at my table. My kids know your name.
lines.tarantino: You ate at my table. My kids know your name. My wife asks after you. That's what you did with all that. That's what you spent it on.
lines.mcdonagh: You sat at my table. Me kids know your name. And you did this anyway. That's the bit I'll never get past.
lines.houser: You've eaten at my table. My children know your name. Whatever they paid you, I hope it was more than that's worth.
lines.coen: You ate at my table. My kids know your name. I don't know what to do with that now.

lines.current: Feels like nobody has been talking to me this week.
lines.why: Three consecutive Willy lines say the same thing three ways ('nobody has said one word', 'looking at me sideways', 'nobody has been talking to me'). The third should escalate into the thing he actually fears, which makes the boat ride unbearable.
lines.house: Nobody's talked to me all week. Am I — is there something I should know? Because I'd rather know.
lines.tarantino: Nobody's talked to me all week. And here's the thing about that. I know what it means when nobody talks to you. I've been on the other end of it. I've been the guy not talking.
lines.mcdonagh: Nobody's talked to me all week. And I know what that means. I've been the fella not talkin' before now.
lines.houser: Nobody's spoken to me in seven days. I've been in this business long enough to know exactly what that is, so somebody say something or turn the boat around.
lines.coen: Nobody's talked to me all week. And I know what that usually means. I'd rather somebody just said it.

lines.current: Your side. Fold it over and hold it down.
lines.why: Flagged as HUD-speak and it is — but it should stay HUD-shaped, because the horror of this beat is that it is being handled as a job. The only fix needed is one crack in Booski's voice somewhere in the sequence.
lines.house: Your side. Fold it over, hold it down. Don't look at the face. I'm telling you now, don't look at the face.
lines.tarantino: Your side. Fold it over, hold it down. And don't look at his face. I'm not saying that to be kind. I'm saying it because you'll see it every night for a year and you've got work tomorrow.
lines.mcdonagh: Your side. Fold it over, hold it down. And don't look at his face. I'm not bein' soft with you, I'm savin' you a year of not sleepin'.
lines.houser: Your side. Fold, hold. Eyes on the tarp, not on him. That's not sentiment, that's just how you stay useful.
lines.coen: Your side there. Fold it over and hold it down. Don't look at his face. Just — don't do that.

lines.why: A confirm button in the middle of the best sequence in the game. Lou has just told him to hold the foyer alone and he answers like he is repeating a lunch order.
lines.house: The stairs. Just me on the stairs. Right.
lines.tarantino: The stairs. Me, on the stairs, on my own. And everybody else is upstairs. I want to make sure I've understood the shape of this.
lines.mcdonagh: The stairs. Me. On me own. On the stairs. Grand. Lovely. That's grand.
lines.houser: The stairs. Alone. While everyone with seniority is above me. I want that architecture noted somewhere.
lines.coen: The stairs. Just me. Okay. Yeah, okay, I've got it.

lines.why: Two words after surviving a siege. There is a whole night's worth of adrenaline with nowhere to go.
lines.house: Sasole. There's a man in a flight jacket on your landing and you want me to go and talk to him.
lines.tarantino: Sasole. Right. There's a man on your landing in a flight jacket. There are forty bodies on your lawn. And the plan is I go and introduce myself.
lines.mcdonagh: Sasole. Right so. There's forty of them on the lawn and a fella in a flight jacket on the landin' and I'm to go and say hello to him.
lines.houser: Sasole. Of course. There's a man in a flight jacket on the landing of a house that's currently a crime scene, and I'm to network.
lines.coen: Sasole. Right. Okay. I'll — yeah. I'll go talk to him.

lines.current: You are the one who held the stairs. Good. Then you can hold a bomb bay.
lines.why: Already good — the flag is a false positive. The only note is that 'Good.' is doing a lot of work; giving Sasole one specific observation makes the recruitment land harder.
lines.house: You're the one who held the stairs. On your own, with a rail and a heavy gun. Then you can hold a bomb bay.
lines.tarantino: You held those stairs. On your own. I watched the last twenty minutes of it from that window and I didn't help, because I wanted to see what you'd do. A man who can hold a staircase can hold a bomb bay.
lines.mcdonagh: You held them stairs. On your own. I watched the last of it from that window and I never lifted a finger, because I wanted to see. You'll do.
lines.houser: You held the stairs. Solo. Against a numerically superior force with better cars. That's exactly the skill set required to stand in an open bomb bay at fifteen thousand feet.
lines.coen: You're the one held the stairs. That's good. That's real good. Then I'd say you can hold a bomb bay.

lines.current: Colton. His grave smells like Asian feet. That is all I have.
lines.why: REWRITE — the crudeness is welcome but the target is wrong. It is the one gag in the game that lands on an ethnicity rather than on a character, which makes it the odd one out in a script that is otherwise cruel about people for things they did. Same joke, better aim.
lines.house: Colton. His grave smells like his van did. Nobody's saying anything but everybody's noticed.
lines.tarantino: Colton. Even the ground smells like his van. Four years underground and he has not managed to become less of a smell.
lines.mcdonagh: Colton. The grave smells like his van did. Dead four year and he's still the worst part of any place he's in.
lines.houser: Colton. His plot smells exactly like his van, which raises questions about the van that nobody wants answered.
lines.coen: Colton. Huh. Smells just like his van did. That's — I don't know what to make of that.

lines.current: That closes the HotDog incident. The Motel does not close this easy.
lines.why: Already strong. One note only: the second half telegraphs the next mission a little cleanly. Variants keep the dread and lose the signposting.
lines.house: That closes the HotDog thing. Get in the car. The next one doesn't close with a shovel.
lines.tarantino: That's HotDog done. Get in the car. The next one doesn't end with a shovel and a hole, and I'd get comfortable with that on the drive.
lines.mcdonagh: That's HotDog closed. Get in the car. The next one doesn't close with a shovel, and you'd want to be thinkin' about that on the way.
lines.houser: That concludes the HotDog matter. Get in the car. The next item does not resolve with earthmoving equipment.
lines.coen: Well. That closes HotDog. Get in the car. The next one's not going to be like this one.

lines.tarantino: [keep as written]
lines.mcdonagh: [keep as written]
lines.houser: [keep as written]
lines.coen: [keep as written]

lines.why: BENCHMARK — the crudest line in the game and the best-earned, because it is doing three jobs at once: the recognition, the threat, and the character. This is the level the owner is asking for everywhere else. Do not touch it.
lines.house: [keep as written]
lines.tarantino: [keep as written]
lines.mcdonagh: [keep as written]
lines.houser: [keep as written]
